Today you will visit the impressive fumaroles of the Tatio geysers. In the language of the indigenous peoples who once inhabited these slopes, "Tatio" means "Weeping Old Man".

The geysers lie more than 4,000 metres above sea level. At sunrise, approximately between 06:00 and 07:00, jets of hot water appear. The excursion starts early so you can greet the dawn at the Tatio geysers, one of the largest and most important geothermal fields in the world.

More than 70 fumaroles release jets of steam, forming pools of boiling water. The most spectacular time is sunrise, when the brilliant blue sky contrasts with white steam rising above the geysers.

A warming breakfast awaits amid this extraordinary natural setting near the Andes. Morning temperatures here can fall to −2 °C.

Next, visit a natural pool where those who wish may bathe in the hot thermal springs of the Cordillera.

On the return journey to San Pedro de Atacama, enjoy the surrounding scenery, valleys, local flora and fauna, including the especially charming vicuñas and viscachas.

Then stop in Machuca, a small Atacameño village consisting of just a few houses built from adobe, straw and cactus wood. Local residents work in tourism, offering Andean handicrafts and traditional foods including llama meat, sopaipillas and empanadas.

You will also visit the beautiful San Santiago Church, dedicated to the village's patron saint, and a small wetland area (*bofedal*) inhabited by flamingos, ducks and other birds.

In a forest area of around 60 hectares, you can see tropical vegetation and, with luck, monkeys, peccaries, birds, insects and other wildlife. Two sections of the trail lead to four waterfalls approximately 15–30 metres high. Along the way, you will need to cross small rivers and rocky stretches.

In clear weather, a viewpoint offers views of Arenal, Rincón de la Vieja, Tenorio and Miravalles, the Guanacaste plains and Lake Arenal. These are panoramic views, not visits to all the places named.

At the end of the route, a light snack is provided by the river, followed by a horseback ride lasting approximately 35 minutes.

## A Day in Nature among the Ventania Hills

We arrange a trip from [Sierra de la Ventana](/argentina/place/sierra-de-la-ventana/) to [Ernesto Tornquist Provincial Park](/argentina/place/ernesto-tornquist-provincial-park/). Accompanied by a guide, we follow a nature trail and climb to viewpoints overlooking rocky slopes and grassy valleys.

For lunch, we stop at a restaurant within the park. After the walk, we return to Sierra de la Ventana, leaving you free to spend the rest of the day at your own pace. The total journey covers approximately 70 km. We will discuss the group's fitness level and a suitable hiking route in advance.
